cover letter
Certified Public Accountant (CPA).
Bachelor's degree, preferably in a related field and/or equivalent experience and/or training.
Advanced degree in related area.

Experience interpreting and applying generally accepted accounting principles, federal regulations, sponsor policies, and university policies governing sponsored research, including the Uniform Guidance (2 C.F.R. Part 200), Federal Acquisition Regulation, and Code of Federal Regulations.
Experience with campus systems, including financial management, payroll/personnel software, data warehouse, and reporting.
Experience in supervising, mentoring, training and evaluating professional staff.
Experience interfacing with auditors and managing compliance for sponsored programs.
Experience in managing a team responsible for a complex and high volume portfolio, including funds management, and ensuring expenditures align with award terms and university policies.
Experience as a seasoned accountant, preferably in a state or university accounting management position.

The Director of Extramural Funds Accounting provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, and expert guidance for the University's extramural accounting activities. The Director manages a team responsible for account set-up in alignment with award terms, institutional funds management, financial reporting, billing and invoicing, revenue management, drawdowns, and closeout of sponsored awards. The role ensures compliance with federal and state regulations, UC policies, cost accounting standards, sponsor terms, and audit requirements. Provides on interpretation of complex policy and award terms, and trains staff to interpret award terms, manage project changes, and ensure compliance.

The Director operates with a high degree of autonomy and is responsible for unit-wide decision-making, ensuring comprehensive and effective fiduciary compliance, and achievement of unit goals and priorities. Manages and mentors a team of financial research administration professionals. Contributes to development, enhancement, and implementation of organization policies governing post-award administration. The Director ensures strong internal controls and serves as a primary financial policy expert in the Office of Research.
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.

The selected candidate will be required to work a hybrid work schedule and must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and fulfill the requirements of the UCSC telecommuting agreement.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

Exercise the utmost discretion in managing sensitive information learned in the course of performing their duties. Sensitive information includes but is not limited to employee and student records, health and patient records, financial data, strategic plans, proprietary information, and any other sensitive or non-public information learned during the course and scope of employment. Understands that sensitive information should be shared on a limited basis and actively takes steps to limit access to sensitive information to individuals who have legitimate business need to know. Ensure that sensitive information is properly safeguarded. Follow all organizational policies and laws on data protection and privacy. This includes secure handling of physical and digital records and proper usage of IT systems to prevent data leaks. The unauthorized or improper disclosure of confidential work-related information obtained from any source on any work-related matter is a violation of these expectations.
Demonstrated knowledge of financial systems and technologies used in accounting and research administration.
Ability to work long periods of time at a computer with or without accommodation.
Demonstrated knowledge of industry best practices in a university environment with the ability to implement and manage broad-based grant management best practices and procedures.
Ability to travel to multiple work locations on and off campus.
Sound judgement and decision making skills.
Ability to maintain appearance and conduct suitable for working in a professional setting.
Strong critical thinking and creative problem-solving skills.
Strong verbal communication skills.
Strong written communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to apply organizational development, strategic planning, change management, and team priority-setting skills to support effective operations and organizational goals.
Demonstrated ability to perform highly complex financial analysis and customized reporting.
Ability to develop unit-wide plans and policies to improve post-award operations and resolve complex compliance or fiscal issues.
